name: Brí Léith

attributes.attribute: a famous fairy mound at the center of Ireland
the palace of Midir, greatest of fairy kings
named for the heroine Brí, possibly another name for Étain

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Part II. Vol. IX. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co. Ltd., 1906. Pp. 3, 299-301.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Brí Léith is a famous fairy mound at the center of Ireland. It was the palace of Midir, the greatest of the fairy kings. Several mythic tales unfold there. Most concern Étain, the reborn heroine and Midir's lover across several lifetimes. The mound carries the name of an obscure heroine called Brí. That name may be another name for Étain.

okr.objective: Describe Brí Léith, the famous central Irish fairy mound.
key_results: Brí Léith was a famous fairy mound in the center of Ireland.
